feature: Private process review record storage and dedicated dashboard

implementation.permission: Owner storage.enabled AND local CLI --save-details; independent of history.enabled/details; show-details alone is not save consent.
implementation.mcp: No new tools/arguments; enabled storage never causes MCP persistence. IDs, names, paths, hashes and record access are omitted.
implementation.store: POSIX pinned directory descriptors, owner-only 0700 directories / 0600 files, no-follow regular owned single-link files, local-filesystem validation, process/thread lock and atomic publication. Windows storage refused.
implementation.retention: Default 7 days; expiry at equality; shortening effective immediately on next operation, original expiry never extended. No background cleanup.
implementation.deletion: Opaque IDs and exact content revision; invalidate private HTML before changes. Expired-record prune also cleans owned orphan temporary files. Dry-run does not delete records but can invalidate stale HTML.
implementation.limits: 2 MiB JSON, 8 MiB HTML, bounded records and combined bytes including temporary files; no unexpired eviction, overwrite on ID collision or automatic save retry.
implementation.states: Collection status and persistence separate; interrupted results not saved; no unverified identity details saved. Dashboard ordered by collection finish, not delayed save time.
implementation.dashboard: Dedicated static private page, native disclosures and internal links, CSP hashed CSS, escaped untrusted text; general history/dashboard never auto-loads process records.

privacy.note: Repository source hashes below identify implementation files only, not inspected personal scripts.

changes: Strict owner/0600/regular-file checks apply to the store's own files only (records, dashboard HTML/JSON, lock, temporary files). Other entries are counted as unmanaged_count in the list, never read, followed, deleted or included in capacity; previously one 0644 file such as Finder's .DS_Store made every later save and the dashboard fail.

A missing folder above the store is treated as no store for list/prune/dashboard (previously a generic error); saving creates nothing and returns save_failed with the fixed persistence_reason store_parent_missing, which the anonymous CLI view also shows.
Stops other than cancel/timeout (read_limit, total_byte_limit, read_limit_or_warning) are not saved and are labelled not_saved_incomplete instead of not_saved_interrupted.
The store folder is fsynced after publishing a record or page and after deletions; a failing folder sync does not turn a published record into save_failed.
